title: Sentinel retail warmup burst characterization labbook
content:
Purpose and context:
This labbook captures an exploratory benchmarking run for Sentinel (retail chat assistant) focused on burst arrivals and the transition to steady-state for our hosted and dedicated deployment options. Customer goal: tolerate occasional 5–10s microbursts (peak QPS) without >2x unit cost increase or >200ms increase in p95 compared to baseline steady traffic.

Scope and test matrix (quick summary):
- Workloads: small-chat (avg tokens 64), medium-summary (avg tokens 220), long-rerank (avg tokens 800).
- Arrival profiles: steady (100 QPS), microburst (single 10s spike to 1800 QPS), sustained ramp (5m ramp 100->600 QPS).
- Models: open-llm-v2-7b (fp16), open-llm-v2-7b-4bit (q4), redwood-chat-13b-llm (fp16).
- Instance types: A100-80G dedicated pool, H100-80G dedicated pool, hosted general pool (mixed).
- Configs: batching target=16/32/64, kv-cache enabled/disabled, prefix-caching on top-k common prompts.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99/token, end-to-end tail latency (client->response-complete), cold-start count, warm-cache hit rate, tokens/sec, tokens-per-dollar, GPU utilization, queue length distribution.

Test environment notes:
- Synthetic user trace generated from Sentinel production logs (anonymized): 7-day sample, weekday evening peak used to seed bursts.
- Traffic driver: locust clusters (eu + us-west) to mimic geo split.
- Time sync: all runners and agents pinned to NTP pool; we used server-side tracing to avoid clock drift in p99 derivation.
- Measurement windows: pre-burst baseline (10m), burst window, cooldown (30m).
- Billing model estimate: used Redwood pricing sheet v2029-09 for hosted token/unit assumptions and reserved pricing for Dedicated A100/H100 pools.

Representative findings (high-level):
- Coldstart behaviour:
  - When a new model container is spun up during the spike, end-to-end coldstart latency added between 2.1s–4.8s depending on model size (13b worst). Median 3.4s.
  - Coldstarts were responsible for ~22% of >1s tails during the first 30s of burst in dedicated clusters without pre-warmed instances.
- Warmup and KV cache:
  - KV cache warmup for conversational tokens materially reduced downstream generator cost after ~6 warm requests per conversation for 220-token sequences. Cache hit rate plateaued at ~85% by 12th request for median sessions.
  - Prefix caching of common prompts (top 40 templates) dropped p95 by ~18% for small-chat workload immediately after cache warming.
- Batching tradeoffs:
  - Large batching (target=64) decreased tokens-per-dollar by 28% in steady state but increased median latency by 160ms and p95 by 420ms under burst conditions due to queue-building at ingress.
  - Dynamic batching with adaptive time-slicing (max-latency 40ms) yielded a better balance: -12% cost vs baseline, p95 penalty <120ms compared to small static batch sizes.
- Hardware differences:
  - H100 pools produced 22–30% lower p99 for long-rerank vs A100 at same concurrency, largely due to faster kernel throughput on long sequences. Cost per token higher for H100 in our pricing model, net cost efficiency depends on workload mix.

Selected quantitative table (representative numbers from single run, long-rerank workload):
- Steady 100 QPS, redwood-chat-13b-llm (fp16) on A100 pool, batching 32:
  - p50: 210ms, p95: 480ms, p99: 860ms, tokens/sec: 9.8k, GPU util: 56%, est tokens-per-dollar: 12.1M
- Burst 10s peak to 1800 QPS (same config), observed during first 30s:
  - p50: 310ms, p95: 1420ms, p99: 3.9s (coldstart spikes), coldstart events: 16, queue length 0->180 in 6s
- Same burst with pre-warmed reserved capacity (scale buffer + warm instances):
  - p50: 220ms, p95: 560ms, p99: 920ms, coldstart events: 1

Cost velocity and unit economics:
- For the small-chat workload, the hosted pool with adaptive batching produced the lowest tokens-per-dollar at our reference usage (steady), but during the burst the hosted plan's burst protection kicked in and the marginal cost per token increased by ~3.7x for the 10s window due to on-demand scaling.
- Dedicated reserved pool with pre-warmed buffer provided the most predictable unit cost during burst (marginal cost change <1.25x) at the expense of committed capacity.

Failure modes observed and root causes:
- Queue flooding at ingress when batching thresholds are large and the admission controller does not apply backpressure quickly enough. Root cause: ingress autoscaler delta + batching window mismatch.
- Cache thrash for highly diverse session IDs (no effective session affinity), leading to lower cache hit rates in sampling experiments. Remediation: session-affinity option in the gateway; prefer conversation pinning when possible.
- Model container spin-up rate limited by image pull throughput on some dedicated nodes (NFS registry throttle observed). Fix: pre-pulled images or use local cache on machines.

Actionable recommendations for Sentinel POC:
- Fast wins (0–2 weeks):
  - Enable prefix-caching for top 30 prompt templates, measure p95 delta in prod-sim.
  - Configure adaptive batching (max-latency 40ms) for small-chat and medium-summary routes.
  - Reserve minimal warm buffer (equivalent to 15 concurrent generator seats) for peak windows; automate warm buffer sizing based on day-of-week.
- Medium term (2–8 weeks):
  - Implement session affinity in gateway for sessions with >3 messages to improve KV cache effectiveness.
  - Add image pre-pull routine to dedicated pool bootstrap to avoid registry-induced coldstarts.
  - Run A/B of A100 vs H100 on mixed workload split (30% long-rerank) to derive blended price/perf curve for their traffic distribution.
- Strategic (quarter+):
  - Explore mixed-precision aggressive quantization for long-rerank path and keep fp16 for chat; if quality delta acceptable, could yield 30–45% cost savings for long calls.
  - Consider predictive scaling based on short-term ML (30s forecast) to pre-warm when microburst probability >45%.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- How tolerant is product to p99 spikes for long-rerank calls that are typically background (can we accept async fallbacks)? Need PM decision.
- Confirm cost model for H100 committed discounts for the customer; current numbers use public list pricing.
- Validate multi-tenant interference on hosted pools for mixed customers; we saw some noise at 95th percentile when other tenants had concurrent spikes.

Appendix: raw artifacts and quick links:
- Locust trace bundle: s3://redwood-lab-results/sentinel/2029-12/warmup-burst-run-20291205.tar.gz
- Trace sampling: span ids and trace view links logged to JIRA SE-4821.
- Short checklist used during experiment: start collectors, validate sample trace, heat baseline 10m, run burst, dump traces, upload metrics CSV.

Notes to self / meeting prep bullets for upcoming customer workshop:
- Show animated chart of queue length vs time during 10s spike (was compelling).
- Bring cost projection table for three operating modes: hosted-on-demand, dedicated-reserved-with-warmbuffer, hybrid (hosted baseline + reserved overflow).
- Decision items for customer: accept small committed buffer? allow async fallback for long-rerank? prioritize H100 for long-call-heavy flows?

End of labbook.

(Author: Asha N. — iterative notes; some figures are from single experiment run and need to be re-run for statistical confidence before inclusion in an external-facing POC report.)
